title: Somatic mutations reveal the ontogeny of microglia in human ageing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py found no PMCID, supplement, accessions or Zenodo/Dryad record. NCBI's PMC link (PMC13446561) turned out to be an unrelated review on CSF1R (a microglia receptor gene) leukoencephalopathy. PMC13228375 is only a stub of the bioRxiv preprint. I read the bioRxiv full text (10.64898/2026.05.19.726366): its data statement says whole-genome sequencing and phenotype data come from ADSP (the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project) via NIAGADS (the National Institute on Aging Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease data service) 'for investigators with approved protocols', and new sequencing will go to dbGaP (NIH's controlled-access genotype database). The Nature page redirected to a login.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything: 20 primary donors (UW1–UW19 plus UW20–UW23), 2 research autopsies, whole-genome sequencing of blood, targeted capture of personal mutation sites, single-nucleus ATAC-seq (a chromatin-accessibility assay) and mitochondrial single-cell ATAC-seq, the 20,379-participant ADSP cohort for the clonal haematopoiesis vs Alzheimer's analysis, and 15 supplementary tables. I did not open any data file.

a1_downloadable.note: Controlled access: the raw sequencing goes to dbGaP and the 20,379-person cohort sits in ADSP/NIAGADS, both needing an approved data-access application (checked in the bioRxiv data statement). Only code is open, on GitHub.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked further after A1 failed. The paper's quantities (fraction of brain cells derived from bone marrow, carrier status for clonal haematopoiesis, the age-related expansion of blood-cell clones) are built from variant calling, not given as a ready column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; the inputs are raw CRAM files (compressed read alignments) behind controlled access.

a5_enough_rows.note: Only 20–23 donors in the brain lineage-tracing part. The 20,379-person part is controlled access. Not verified in files.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw whole-genome sequencing data; not checked further.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked; no files are accessible.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked. Clonal haematopoiesis calls come from a variant-calling pipeline.

honest_claim_h3: No model claim is possible without controlled-access data. The open part is roughly 20 donors' summary values, which is too few to train on.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's blood mutation profile and age to predict how much of their brain's immune-cell pool came from bone marrow.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-donor blood whole-genome mutations and clone sizes. Only about 20 donors have brain measurements (paper text, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of brain microglia (the brain's resident immune cells) that came from bone marrow, measured by tracking shared somatic mutations (mutations acquired after birth) with targeted capture sequencing.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would tell Alzheimer's researchers who is likely to have many blood-derived brain immune cells. But about 20 donors with controlled-access data makes it infeasible.

ml_idea: None feasible. The sequencing and cohort data sit behind dbGaP and NIAGADS access applications, and the brain lineage-tracing part has only about 20 donors.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement: controlled access through dbGaP and NIAGADS (done).

verdict_reason: Rejected at A1: the sequencing goes to dbGaP and the 20,379-person cohort is in ADSP/NIAGADS, both controlled access needing an approved application. The open brain lineage data covers only about 20 donors.
